A lazy subset that stays lazy (and sparse)

Source: R/altarr.R
altarr_view.Rd

altarr_view(x, i, j, k) is x[i, j, k, drop = FALSE] as a new lazy array: nothing is read when it is made. Its chunks have the same shape as x's, laid over the subset, and each is read with one altarr_extract() of x. If x has a chunk index (present), the view gets one too: a view chunk is absent when every chunk of x it draws from is absent, so a subset of a sparse array is still sparse, and sum() of it is still answered from the index for the empty parts.

Usage

altarr_view(x, ...)

Arguments

x

an altarr array

...

one subscript per dimension (missing means all)

Value

a lazy array (an altarr), with dim the lengths of the subscripts. Dimnames are kept.

Details

This is what an ArraySubset ALTREP method could return instead of a dense result: a method that receives x[i, j, k]'s normalized subscripts can hand back any vector, including another lazy one.

Examples

x <- altarr_zarr_v2(altarr_example_zarr(sparse = TRUE))
v <- altarr_view(x, 1:50, , 1:10)
is_altarr(v)
#> [1] TRUE
sum(altarr_present(v)); length(altarr_present(v))
#> [1] 6
#> [1] 24
all.equal(sum(v, na.rm = TRUE), sum(x[1:50, , 1:10], na.rm = TRUE))
#> [1] TRUE
